findings.text: follow-on: the concurrency test does not fail when the lock it names is reverted — with _locked reduced to a passthrough in a scratch copy it passed 20 of 20 runs (and 10 of 10 with the lock present), so a regression that removes the lock is not caught; the timing assertion `assert not finished.wait(timeout=0.2)` at this line is satisfied in both states.

follow-on: the docstring claims the reentrant _PROCESS_LOCK keeps a nested same-thread call from deadlocking on the file lock, but a reentrant lock admits the nested call, which then opens a second descriptor and blocks on flock; the stated purpose is the inverse of what the code does and no lock here is non-reentrant.

follow-on: the manifest's artifacts gate and evidence_inputs still read base 152 passed / head 158 passed while its own baseline_suite and after_suite fields and the gate logs record 205 and 212, so a reader trusting the summary is misled about the run's gate population.

item_verdicts.diff: read the single gained commit 6b8d37db1: it removes the available parameter from _scale_for_banked_reset so reset_available is added only when a reset is counted, wraps the three store writers in a new _locked context manager, adds a _same_observation early return, and adds one concurrency test.
item_verdicts.done_when: done_when item 2 asks the reading carry reset_available and the pace reflect the extra window; tests/test_codex_banked_reset.py:84-104 asserts reset_available is absent without a flag and that the derived and effective_limit double and burn halves with one; the manifest records the gate over the named files.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that a banked codex reset adds one window of allowance until used; the gained commit serialises every store read-check-write under a lock (reckon/crew/budget_reset.py:69-87) and keeps a no-flag group's allowance byte-identical (reckon/budget.py:1977), both repairing that mechanism.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records base 205 EXIT=0 and head 212 EXIT=0 in its suite fields but its artifacts and evidence_inputs prose still say 152/158, contradicting its own gate logs.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node was fenced to reckon/budget.py, reckon/cli.py, reckon/crew/budget_reset.py, tests/test_codex_banked_reset.py and two doc paths; the gained diff 44636a5f0..6b8d37db1 lists exactly the first, third and fourth.

justifications.durability: tests/test_codex_banked_reset.py:90 fails if reset_available is set for a no-flag group, but the concurrency test at :162-219 passed 20 of 20 runs in a scratch copy with _locked reduced to a passthrough and 10 of 10 with the lock present, so it does not distinguish the two and the lock change it names is effectively unguarded.
justifications.evidence: gate-head.log records 212 passed EXIT=0 at 6b8d37db and gate-base.log 205 passed EXIT=0 at 5b947ae9, but the reviewed manifest's artifacts and evidence_inputs prose still reports 152/158, so two of its own numbers disagree with its logs.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/budget_reset.py:69-87 follows the flock contextmanager idiom of reckon/ledger.py:1251, but its docstring says the reentrant _PROCESS_LOCK stops a nested call deadlocking when a reentrant lock is exactly what admits the nested call that then blocks on a second flock.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/budget.py:1983 adds reset_available only when credit>0 and reckon/crew/budget_reset.py:155-247 hold one lock across the store's read-check-write, so a no-flag group stays replay-equal and a concurrent clear cannot be resurrected.
justifications.reuse: the lock reuses fcntl.flock as the repo's other per-module lock helpers do; reckon/_store.py:315 _serialized_path_lock is the nearest owner but is private and keyed differently, so this extends the idiom and forks no shared capability.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff over 44636a5f0..6b8d37db1 changes only reckon/budget.py, reckon/crew/budget_reset.py and tests/test_codex_banked_reset.py, all inside the declared write paths.
